clue.text: Capital of the vegetable kingdom ?

parts.note: a capital city that also lends its name to a familiar green vegetable, the small sprouts, so it could rule a kingdom of vegetables

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about which city reigns over the world of vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is the capital of Belgium, and its name is also borne by the small cabbage-like sprouts eaten with Christmas dinner in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian capital shares its name with a well-known sprout, so it is the capital city of vegetables too.

clue.text: Unsubstantial product of inflation

parts.note: blowing air into soapy film gives a hollow sphere, and an economic boom of inflated prices is called the same thing

explanation.surface: An economist's sniff at the empty results of rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflation' reads as economics, but it also means simply blowing up with air; both readings give the same fragile, hollow thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap globe is made by inflating and has no substance; a speculative boom shares the word.

clue.text: 26 clamour'

parts.note: the answer to 26 across means rising, and up is a short word for rising
a clamour is a loud roar

explanation.surface: A bare cross-reference: the clue borrows its first word from another light.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 across is RISING; read 'rising clamour' and each half gives a piece, while the whole phrase also describes a growing din.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising clamour is a loud tumult, which is the meaning of the word.

clue.text: As one might put it colloquially

definitions.text: As one might put it colloquially

parts.words: As one might put it colloquially
parts.note: a stock phrase a speaker adds to flag an expression as informal or figurative

explanation.surface: A speaker apologising for an informal turn of phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to mark a manner of speaking that is loose or figurative rather than literal.

clue.text: Even these men 'of high standing have come down to earth

definitions.text: Even these men 'of high standing have come down to earth

parts.words: Even these men 'of high standing have come down to earth
parts.note: people of high social standing who own estates; their first word means come down to earth, as a plane does, and also means owning land

explanation.surface: A remark that even the grandest people have been humbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come down to earth' looks like being humbled, but it is the literal sense of touching down, while also hinting at owning land; 'men of high standing' are the upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: Landowning upper-class families form a social class whose name pairs a word for touched down with a word for gentlefolk.

clue.text: They are plainly indicated on maps of S America

definitions.text: They are plainly indicated on maps of S America

parts.words: They are plainly indicated on maps of S America
parts.note: 'plainly' means as plains: the vast grasslands of Argentina are marked as plains on a map of the continent

explanation.surface: A geography lesson about features clearly shown on South American maps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plainly' seems to mean clearly, but it means as plains: the great treeless grasslands of Argentina and Uruguay.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American grasslands are flat, treeless plains, which a map marks as such.

clue.text: Scent of a rambler rose, .say?

parts.note: a rambler is a roamer, and 'a roamer' spoken in a non-rhotic accent sounds like the word for a pleasant smell such as a rose gives off

explanation.surface: A gardener sniffing a climbing rose.
explanation.walkthrough: A rambler rose is a climbing rose, but a rambler is also a roamer, and 'a roamer', said in British English with no R sound, gives the word for a scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant smell, such as that given off by a climbing rose, is a fragrance or perfume.

clue.text: A strip to distress these good subjects

indicators.note: to distress something is to rough it up, so the letters before it are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is ordered to strip and upset some loyal subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distress' sits as a verb, but it is the anagram signal on A STRIP TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Good subjects of a country are loyal to it, as people who love their homeland are.

clue.text: Where Yum Yum and her companions came from

definitions.text: Where Yum Yum and her companions came from

parts.words: Where Yum Yum and her companions came from
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's Mikado, Yum-Yum and her friends sing that they are three little maids from school, a girls' boarding school

explanation.surface: A question about the origins of an operetta heroine and her friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Yum-Yum is a schoolgirl in The Mikado, the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera; she and her friends are 'three little maids from school', an old-fashioned girls' academy.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a private school or academy for young ladies, as in the opera's girls' school.

clue.text: One has first to exclude Italian singer

indicators.note: says the word one is preceded by the other pieces, so they stand in front of it

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone must first shut out an Italian opera star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One has first' means ONE has BAR and IT placed before it; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice between tenor and bass, and so a kind of singer.

clue.text: Piperson beaten ?

definitions.meaning: the nursery rhyme hero '..., the piper's son', printed here run together, who stole a pig and was beaten
a hand drum that is beaten is named after its sound

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme boy getting his punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs 'Piper's son' together. In the rhyme, the piper's son stole a pig and was beaten; the hyphenated name is also a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme names the boy twice over, and that doubled name is also a small drum played by hand.

clue.text: Sharp pains it might induce — but on one side only!

indicators.note: says the letters before it could be brought about in another arrangement, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bias that brings on sharp pains, but only on one side of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp pains' reads as a medical symptom felt on one side, but SHARP PAINS IT is the fodder for the anagram signalled by 'might induce'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias in favour of one faction means taking one side only.

clue.text: They may be of interest, to those who make them

definitions.text: They may be of interest, to those who make them

parts.words: They may be of interest, to those who make them
parts.note: money lent out earns interest for the lender, so it is of interest in the money sense

explanation.surface: Something that intrigues the people who produce it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of interest' looks like intriguing, but it means earning interest, which money lent out does for the lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Sums lent out earn interest for the lender, who makes them.

clue.text: A coming-out display

parts.note: a coming out is a flowing forth, as light or a gas issues from a source

explanation.surface: A debutante's grand entrance into society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming-out' suggests a debutante's ball, but it means issuing forth, as rays or vapours do from a source.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that flows out from a source, such as light or vapour, is a coming forth.

clue.text: He raises many pounds by his activities

definitions.text: He raises many pounds by his activities

parts.words: He raises many pounds by his activities
parts.note: a fundraiser raises pounds sterling, but this athlete raises pounds in weight above his head

explanation.surface: A charity worker who brings in large sums through events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raises many pounds' sounds like fundraising in sterling, but the pounds are weight lifted by an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete who hoists heavy barbells lifts many pounds in weight.

clue.text: Complaint of those living in Nuneaton?

definitions.text: Complaint of those living in Nuneaton

parts.words: Complaint of those living in Nuneaton
parts.note: Nuneaton, an English Midlands town, said aloud sounds like 'none eaten', and eating nothing brings on exhaustion from want of food

explanation.surface: A question about an illness peculiar to one English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuneaton is a town in Warwickshire; its name sounds like 'none eaten', and the complaint is weakness from starvation.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for exhaustion caused by lack of nourishment, a condition or ailment.

clue.text: Man's man admits behaving calumniously

parts.note: a man admitting something speaks in the first person, saying I
to behave calumniously is to spread false and damaging talk, that is, to slander

explanation.surface: A fellow confesses to spreading malicious lies.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is an island, so a Man's man lives on an island. The man's admission reads 'I slander'.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Isle of Man lives on an island.

clue.text: They are the outcome of faulty distribution

definitions.text: They are the outcome of faulty distribution

parts.words: They are the outcome of faulty distribution
parts.note: distribution here is the dealing of playing cards, and a faulty one must be redone

explanation.surface: A complaint about things going wrong when goods are shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distribution' suggests goods or wealth, but it is the dealing of a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongly dealt hands of cards come from distributing the pack badly.

clue.text: Amid the sands, choose a vessel that's spotless

indicators.note: means the next piece goes in the middle of the word for the sands, splitting it open

parts.note: taken as written, the word sands
to pick is to choose
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: Someone on a beach selects a boat that is perfectly clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amid' puts PICK inside SANDS, after its first letter: S-PICK-ANDS; then PAN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning perfectly clean and tidy, without a mark.

clue.text: As mild as it might be depressing

indicators.note: says the letters before it are shown as they could be in another order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Something gentle that could still be gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it might be' signals an anagram of AS MILD.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and dreary, as something depressing is.

clue.text: Successful boxers aren't out for these titles

definitions.text: Successful boxers aren't out for these titles

parts.words: Successful boxers aren't out for these titles
parts.note: a floored boxer who wins does not stay down for the referee's ten, and the same word is also a nobleman's title

explanation.surface: Winning boxers are not after championship belts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out for' looks like seeking, but it means being knocked out for the referee's tally of ten seconds; the word also names noblemen, so 'titles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Continental noblemen hold a title equivalent to an earl, and the word also means the referee's tallies.

clue.text: A real band with variety star

indicators.note: variety means a changed form, so these letters are rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: A genuine band on a variety bill with a headline performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' suggests a variety show with a star turn, but it signals an anagram of A REAL BAND; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The bright red giant in Taurus is a named star, the eye of the bull.

clue.text: The staff, advised not to make a declaration

definitions.meaning: a short stick or rod, such as a conductor's or relay runner's

definitions.text: advised not to make a declaration
definitions.meaning: in cricket a captain may declare an innings closed

explanation.surface: Office workers are warned not to make any statement.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cricket: a declaration closes an innings early, so a side told to keep batting is told 'bat on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod or stick is a staff; and the cricket instruction to keep batting rather than declare.

clue.text: He announces his intention to take the plunge

definitions.text: He announces his intention to take the plunge

parts.words: He announces his intention to take the plunge
parts.note: a man diving in might say '...', which run together is a man's name, as in the architect Jones

explanation.surface: A bold man declaring he is about to commit himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the plunge' suggests a big decision, but it is literal diving; 'in I go' run together is a Spanish-derived man's name, borne by the architect Jones.
explanation.definitionFit: The man's name, read as three words, is exactly what a diver says before jumping in.

clue.text: Scarcity of ravelled thread .

indicators.note: ravelled thread is tangled, so its letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A shortage of tangled yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravelled' signals an anagram of THREAD; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage or lack, as scarcity is.

clue.text: Professors for presidents ?

parts.note: a professor holds a university chair, so people with chairs are those who preside over meetings

explanation.surface: Proposing academics as heads of state.
explanation.walkthrough: A professor holds a 'chair', so professors are literally chair men; those who preside over meetings bear the same title.
explanation.definitionFit: People who preside over committees or companies are their presidents.

clue.text: Revolt seen daily in the East

definitions.meaning: a revolt is an uprising or rebellion
the sun comes up in the east every morning

explanation.surface: A rebellion reported every day from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The East' looks political, suggesting unrest, but it is just the compass point where the sun comes up each day.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurrection is an uprising; and the sun is seen coming up in the east each morning.

clue.text: They 'do mill-owners many a good turn.

definitions.text: They 'do mill-owners many a good turn

parts.words: They 'do mill-owners many a good turn
parts.note: a good turn is a favour, but in a textile mill the rods that twist yarn literally turn many times

explanation.surface: Something that keeps doing favours for factory bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good turn' looks like a favour, but the rods in a spinning mill really do turn, over and over, to wind thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating rods on spinning machines wind thread in a textile mill.
